sentences.text: 1 This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 19-07-2023 at about 9.15 a.m., the Petitioner was doing house keeping work on 15th Cross road, near water tank playground, K.S.Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of a Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-H-9768 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately shifted to Vasavi Hospital, wherein after first aid, she was admitted to Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru, as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that the Petitioner has spent huge amount for treatment,
medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 52 years,
working as a house keeper in BBMP and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, she has lost her earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insurer and Respondent No.2-Insured.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

4. The respondent no.1 has filed its written statement and denied the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.

It has contended that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It has contended that the rider of offending vehicle was not having valid DL, offending vehicle had no valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him,
expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him.
Further contended that the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive and unreasonable.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained injuries in an accident when she was doing the house keeping work on 15 th Cross road, near water tank playground,
K.S.Layout, Bengaluru District on 19-7- 2023 about 9.15 a.m. only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-13-H-9768?
2.
What compensation petitioner is entitled ?

Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 19-07-2023 at about 9.15 a.m., she was sweeping at 15th Cross road, near water tank playground, K.S.Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of a Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-H-9768 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

10. In order to substantiate her case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 7 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, and charge sheet.

As per wound certificate petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Punctured wound over medial aspect of left ankle.
2. Swelling and tenderness over left ankle.
3. Abnormal mobility left ankle.
4. Left ankle Bimalleolar fracture with subluxation of ankle with syndesmotic injury.
11.
The respondent No.2 has contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of the petitioner and on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.1 to Ex.P 7 i.e., police records establish that the accident had occurred on 19-7-2023 at about 9.15 a.m. when she was sweeping at 15th Cross road, near water tank playground, K.S.Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of a Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-13-H- 9768 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Since the respondents have not challenged the police documents.
12. It is stated that the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending vehicle.
In this regard Kumarswamy Layout traffic police registered a case in Cr.No.327/2023 for the offence punishable U/s.279 and 337 of IPC in which he has been charge sheeted.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination of PW-1 nothing favorable to the respondent is extracted.
Except cross- examination and contention in the objections, respondent no 1-insurance company has not produced any evidence to disprove the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle 14.
By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of rider of offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
Charge sheet prima-facie establishes the rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injury in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle.

15. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Punctured wound over medial aspect of left ankle.
2. Swelling and tenderness over left ankle.
3. Abnormal mobility left ankle.
4.
Left ankle Bimalleolar fracture with subluxation of ankle with syndesmotic injury.
The doctor opined that the injury No.2 is simple in nature and other injuries are grievous in nature.
16. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately she was taken to Vasavi hospital, Bengaluru, wherein after first aid, thereafter she was admitted in Sanjaygandhi hospital as inpatient and underwent surgery.
She has stated that at the time of accident, she was a sweeper in BBMP and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries she has suffered loss of income.
She has lost her normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

17. The Petitioner has examined Dr. Shekar M., an Orthopedic Surgeon at Sanjaygandhi hospital,
Bengaluru, as Pw-2 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.16 to 18.
18.

PW-2 has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated at Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru and Petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Punctured wound over medial aspect of left ankle.
2. Swelling and tenderness over left ankle.
3. Abnormal mobility left ankle.
4. Left ankle Bimalleolar fracture with subluxation of ankle with syndesmotic injury.

sentences.text: has stated that she was admitted in the Sanjaygandhi hospital and treated with ORIF with plate and screws and for medial malleolus with tension band wiring.
Syndesmotic screws were also put.
Post operatively she was immobilized with below knee POP slab on left side.
PW-2 has examined the Petitioner clinically and radiologically while assessing disability.

He found that Petitioner complains of moderate pain in left ankle, difficulty in walking, sitting cross legged,
squatting, restricted movement of left ankle.
He has assessed the total physical disability of the left leg at 49.71% and whole body disability at 16.57%.
20. PW-2 in his cross-examination has stated that he has treated the Petitioner.
He stated that the petitioner got leg injury but two bones were fractured.
He has given follow-up treatment to the petitioner.
He stated that the petitioner can do his day to day activities with difficulties.
It is pertinent to note that PW2 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

21. Therefore, considering that the grievous injury and considering the difficulties, avocation and evidence of PW-2 and also by considering the age of the Petitioner, the functional disability is assessed at 8%.

22. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 52 years, Wherein Ex.P.10 Aadhar card shows that she was born on 01-01-1971, the same is considered as age of the petitioner as on the date of accident as 52 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 11.
23.
Due to the accident she has sustained grievous injuries.
She was admitted in Sanjaygandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was treated as an inpatient from 19-07-2023 to 01-08-2023.
She has stated that at the time of accident, she was sweeper at BBMP and was earning Rs.18,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to do her work and is unable to do her work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
The petitioner has produced her BBMP ID card at Ex.P.11, but she has not produced her pay slip.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the notional income chart of the Lok Adalath.
24. The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2023, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 16,000/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
25. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.

As the Petitioner is a house keeper at BBMP,
considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 8%.

Thus loss of future income comes to Rs.16,000 x 12 x 11 x 8 /100= Rs.1,68,960/-
towards loss of future income.

26. Pain and sufferings: So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and was inpatient for a period of 14 days which caused her to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .20,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.

sentences.text: Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in her day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .15,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
28. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to .30,868/-
The Respondent has not seriously disputed the medical bills.
On perusal of medical bills it appears that the petitioner has spent Rs 30,868 towards medical expenses.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of 30,868/- towards Medical Expenses.
29. Future medical expenses:
PW-2 Doctor has stated that Petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants which cost around Rs.25,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation report.
In the absence of clear evidence, it is just and reasonable to award .15,000/- towards future medical expenses.
30. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.8-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at Sanjaygandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient from 19-07-2023 to 01-08- 2023 .i.e, for a period of 14 days.

Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .15,000/- under the head of conveyance, food,
nourishment and attendant charges.
31. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 14 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 2 months for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 2 months.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 2 = 32,000/-.
32.

sentences.text: Liability:

The Respondent no 1-insurance company has denied its liability only on the ground that the rider of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and that RC owner has handed over the vehicle to minor and it was the violation of the condition of the policy.
34. Respondent No.2 RC owner has not contested the case by producing cogent evidence.
Insurance company examined its official as RW-1.
Charge sheet filed against the rider of the offending for the offence punishable under section 279,338,IPC section 181 IMV Act.
Ex P7 establishes that rider of offending vehicle was not holding DL at time of the accident and he was a minor.
The RC owner knowingly had handed over the vehicle to minor.
35. RW-1 has deposed that the Insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in view of violation of terms of insurance contract.
36. In the present case admittedly insurance covers the third party risk.
The insurance policy is a contract executed between the owner and the insurer.

In the present case though the insurance was valid as on the date of accident, the respondent no 2 knowingly handed over possession of the vehicle to a rider who was minor and did not hold a valid and effective driving licence for the offending vehicle.
It is the willful breach of terms of contract of insurance.

37. Petitioner requested to order for pay and recovery as it is the case of injury to third party and relied upon the following decisions:
MFA No 5033/2014 between Satheesh vs Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co Ltd and others.
2024 ACJ 2816 between Rajannna and another V Abhasaheb and another.
38.

entities.text: Satheesh vs Bajaj Alliance General Insurance Co Ltd and others.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By considering the above said Judgment and the available materials on record, The amendment to Motor Vehicle Act was brought on 19-07-2022.
Motor Vehicle Act being a substantive law, the amendment brought to it operates prospectively.
Hence the amendment has no application to the case on hand.
Therefore the order of pay and recovery is not applicable to this case.

39. Although the insurance was valid on the date of accident, the respondent no 2 knowingly handed over possession of the vehicle to a rider who was minor and did not hold a valid and effective driving licence for the offending vehicle.
This constitutes a willful breach of the terms of the insurance contract.
Hence, Respondent no 2 being owner of the offending vehicle shall pay compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. to the Petitioner.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
40. ISSUE NO.3 :

2, I proceed to pass the following:
